This name would have been given to a child to inspire a sense of bravery and toughness. In some contexts, it could also serve as a name for a military leader or a fighter.

historical_references.reference: Chargul was an important trade center in the Islamic world, located at the crossroads of major caravan routes. It is believed to have been the site of a major caravanserai and marketplace during the Abbasid Caliphate (750-1258 AD).

Chargul is also mentioned in the travels of Ibn Battuta, a 14th-century Moroccan scholar and traveler. He described it as a prosperous town with a large market and a mosque that was famous for its beautiful architecture.
